source.title: NeuronScope: A Multi-Agent Framework for Explaining Polysemantic Neurons in Language Models
source.authors: Wei-Qi Liu; Yongliang Miao; Hai-Yan Zhao; Yan-Guang Liu; Mengnan Du

record.file_problem: No major text problem; minor PDF-to-text formatting artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures the number of semantic concepts associated with selected language-model neurons using its own decomposition and clustering method, rather than the original sources’ methods.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports Number, defined as the number of distinct semantic concepts associated with a neuron, for selected layers and models. These are means over analyzed neurons, not proportions of neurons; the study does not directly establish that the reported concepts are unrelated. The score improvements concern explanation faithfulness, not polysemanticity, so they are not rows. The paper’s cited claims about polysemanticity are not counted as results.
record.test_reason: This is a neuron-explanation method paper. It takes polysemanticity as given, citing Olah 2020 and Elhage 2022, and reports its own pipeline's performance. The only polysemanticity-like number is 'Number', the count of HDBSCAN clusters (minimum size 2) of GPT-4o-generated explanation fragments. That is a property of the explanation pipeline, not a direct measure of a neuron responding to unrelated tokens. The paper's own examples (Table 3, App. G) show clusters that are often paraphrases or offshoots of one concept, such as city names, 'common/traits', and '#' comment syntax. Neurons were also selected as the 200 with the highest activation frequency per layer. So Number cannot show the share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated inputs (V2). It is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that NeuronScope 'uncovers hidden polysemanticity' and that activation-guided refinement raises the simulator correlation score by about 0.05–0.10 over the single-pass variant. Note that the polysemanticity claim rests on explanation-cluster counts and case-study visualizations, not on an independent prevalence measure.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses high-activation text examples, agent-generated decomposition and clustering, and iterative simulator-scored refinement; it does not apply the original sources’ neuron-analysis methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported Number aggregates vary across model and layer. The study also reports dependence on the quality and diversity of activation samples as a limitation.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean number of HDBSCAN clusters of GPT-4o explanation fragments per neuron, over the 200 highest-activation-frequency neurons per layer. Llama-3.1-8B: 4.48–5.53. Gemma-2-2B: 2.22–2.49. Qwen3-4B: 2.26–2.42. There is no consistent layer trend. The examples show many clusters are near-paraphrases of one concept.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM-generated neuron explanations, decomposed and clustered, yield multiple explanation clusters per neuron. The number varies by model more than by layer.

record.problems: The semantic concept counts are generated through the proposed explanation pipeline and are reported as aggregates, not neuron-level distributions or prevalence estimates. The analysis selects 200 neurons with the highest activation frequency per selected layer. The study does not independently establish that counted concepts are unrelated. It notes that clustering may be sensitive to activation-sample quality and diversity.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 Score values are omitted because they measure explanation prediction faithfulness, not the prevalence or degree of polysemantic neuron responses. Qualitative appendix examples are not separately cataloged as they are illustrations of generated explanations or clustering rather than independent quantified prevalence results.

untested.parts: No share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts. No verification that clusters are unrelated. Only 200 selected neurons per layer.
No initialization, regularization or noise test.
No test of whether mixtures reduce to one shared feature.
No comparison of activation ranges or scoring choices for classifying neurons.

record.verdict_notes: The paired rows (w/o Refinement vs. full) carry identical Number values by construction, so the method condition is uninformative; the comparator rows are redundant. The record's 'supports' V2 label is removed: a cluster count from an LLM explanation pipeline with minimum cluster size 2 does not establish unrelated responses or their share among neurons.

versions.untested_parts: Vision models and the InceptionV1 neuron example are not tested.

The study reports mean concept counts for selected high-activation-frequency neurons, but not the share of all MLP neurons that respond to unrelated inputs. It does not independently verify that the concepts counted are unrelated, or compare raw neuron-response rates across layers.
No test of superposition or feature-to-neuron capacity pressure.
No test of initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity.
No comparison of activation functions, architectures, or regularization effects on the share of polysemantic neurons, and no performance-cost test.
The study does not test whether canonical mixtures are actually one shared feature or related offshoots, nor estimate how often truly unrelated mixtures occur.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation-scoring choices as determinants of whether a neuron counts as polysemantic.

rows.measure: Number of distinct semantic concepts per neuron (table aggregate)
rows.note: The aggregate is above one, consistent with multiple assigned concepts, but does not give the fraction of neurons with multiple concepts or establish that they are unrelated.
rows.check: Number counts clusters of LLM explanation fragments, not unrelated activation contexts. It is a mean over 200 selected high-frequency neurons, not a share of neurons. The w/o-Refinement row duplicates r2 because Number is computed before refinement.
